Civil Revision No.2706 of 2009
lawyer:
Mr. Sherder Abul Hossain, Advocate ------- For the petitioner 
Mr. Md. Kamrul Alam (Kamal), Advocate -------- For the Opposite Parties No.1-8

Md. Abul Kalam Azad ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioner
-Vs-

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 16.06.2009 and 22.06.2009 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in allowing the Title Appeal No.33 of 2006 along with Title Appeal No.40 of 2006 analogously and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2006 and 09.04.2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in decreeing the Title Suit No.14 of 2001 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

	2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No.14 of 2001 in the 2nd Court of learned Joint District Judge, Chandpur against the defendants for a decree of specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property contending inter alia that the suit property originally belonged to the defendant Narayan Proshad Mondol, who proposed the plaintiff to buy the property and the plaintiff agreed to purchase the same. Accordingly, on 15.05.1984 the consideration amount of the land was fixed at Tk.3,75,000/- and it was settled that on 27.05.1984 out of the total consideration amount, Tk. 3,60,000/- will be paid by the plaintiff for getting a deed of agreement. Accordingly, the plaintiff by the date fixed paid Tk.3,60,000 in favour of the defendant and accordingly the defendant after taking the amount, executed a deed of agreement in favour of the plaintiff and handover possession of the suit property. It was agreed by the parties that after payment of the rest amount of Tk.15,000/- the plaintiff will obtain the sub-kabala deed from the defendant. Thereafter; the plaintiff on several occasions going before the defendant requested him to take the remaining money of consideration and execute and register the sub-kabala deed, but the defendant showing different excuse requested the plaintiff to wait. Last of all, on 05.02.2001 the plaintiff accompanied by his witnesses went to the residence of the defendant to pay the remaining amount of Tk.15,000/-, at which; the defendant told the plaintiff to come on 14.02.2001 at Hajiganj with an undertaking that on the following day he will execute and register a sub-kabala deed in the concerned registry office. But on the date fixed the defendant did not go there, and finding no other alternative the plaintiff instituted the original suit for specific performance of contract. 

	3. The contrary case of the defendant in short is thus that the defendant Narayan Prosad Mondal @ Narayan Chandra Mondal was the owner of the suit property by way of a sole decree among the co-sharers on 06.03.1968 pursuant to a Partition Suit being No.367 of 1967. The further case of the defendant is such that the plaintiff in collusion with one Jitu Mia created a false hainapatra and Jitu Mia in the name of an Ammoktarnama deed after taking signature of the defendant on false representation helped the plaintiff. That Jitu Mia behind the back of the defendant filed a partition suit against the defendants No.3-8 and subsequently withdrawn the same with a permission to sue afresh. The defendant No. 01 Narayan Prosad in finding a notice from the Bureau of Anti-Corruption for the first time came to learn about that deed of agreement(bainapatra). The defendant apprehends that Jitu Mia at the time of execution of the Ammoktarnama obtained his signatures in another paper by which the bainanama was created. The defendant No.1 denied the case of the plaintiffs that he wanted to sale the suit property and entered into a deed of agreement. The defendant No. 01 further alleged that Jitu Mia against the will of the defendant No.1 on 10.09.2001 filed a written statement collusively and filed a `solenama' and knowing that, the defendant No. 01 Narayan Chandra on 11.10.2001 cancelled the Ammoktarnama which was given in favour of Jitu Mia. 

	4. The case of the defendants No.3-8 in a nutshell is such that the predecessor of the present defendants, one Ali Ahmed Patwary purchased .42 acres of land from the co-sharers of the suit holding on 10.05.1967 and filed a Civil Suit No.704 of 1979 in the 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge and obtained a decree on 04.12.1981. Besides this; the other co-sharers by two sale deeds dated 04.02.1967 and 06.03.1967 sold out .50 acres of land of the suit holding in favour of Ali Ahmed Patwary, and that the other co-sharers of the suit holding by a `heba' deed dated 12.12.1979 transferred some land in favour of Ali Ahmed Patwary, and Ali Ahmed also obtained some land by a sole decree in partition Suit No.367 of 1967 and after the death of Ali Ahmed Patwary the present defendants became his heirs and obtained his land. It is further case of these defendants that the defendant No. l transferred the suit land in favour of their predecessor Ali Ahmed Patwary and thereby the defendant No.1 had no land in the suit holding which can be transferred to the plaintiff. 

	5. In the original suit, the government of Bangladesh, who was the defendant No. 2 contested the suit and the case of the defendant No.2 is such that the original owners of the suit property migrated to India and as such the property has become vested and non-resident property under the government. 

	6. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by its judgment and decree .dated 30.03.2006. 

	7. Being aggrieved the defendant No.1 filed Title Appeal No.33 of 2006 and the defendants No. 3-8 filed Title Appeal No. 40 of 2006 in the court of learned District Judge, Chandpur which were transmitted to the Court of learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur for hearing and disposal and the learned appellate court taking analogous hearing of both the two appeals, allowed the same and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 16.06.2009. 

	8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner has preferred both two civil revision applications under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

	9. During hearing of this Rules Mr. Sherder Abul Hossain, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Kamrul Alam (Kamal) the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 

	10. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeals committed gross illegality and, irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur committed error of law in allowing the appeals without controverting the findings of the trial court according to the provisions of Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned Appellate Court gave perverse findings that it is admitted by the seller that he had already transferred his entire share to the 3rd party before the alleged contract for sale. The learned counsel submits that the executant of the contract, did not willfully gave evidence before the court and in the pretext of his false illness that he is dumb and deaf he did not appear before the trial Court, and in this context the learned trial court in his observation and findings in the order sheet clearly opined that the defendant No.1 is a physically sound person and capable of giving evidence but the learned Appellate Court failed to consider that material facts on record, and thereby committed gross illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and that the defendant No.1 has played a foul play in the court, which is against the principle of equity and justice. The learned Advocate also submits that a suit for specific performance of contract is an equitable relief, which is guided by the principle of equity, but the learned Additional District Judge has totally failed to appreciate the actual proposition of law and arrived at an erroneous decision as to the merit of the appeals. The learned Advocate argued that the cause of action of the suit arose on 15.02.2001, when the defendant No.1 by his conduct and dealing expressed his denial to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff, and from that date the original suit was filed within time. The learned Advocate also argued that the learned Appellate Court surprisingly made a comment in the impugned judgment and decree that the papers in which the deed of agreement was written are anti-dated, but in fact; the papers in which the deed of agreement was written were not anti-dated and manipulated, rather; the defendant No.1 to the original suit at his free consent and will; executed the same as a "bainanama " in favour of the plaintiff and that the possession was also delivered much earlier and the plaintiff after taking possession over the suit property started to reside therein and that the order-sheets of the trial court; makes it clear that the conduct of the defendant No.1 is not at all satisfactory; rather he has played a foul play with the court. The learned Advocate during his argument argued that the defendant No.1 who was the admitted owner of the suit property categorically admitted his signature in the deed of agreement and as a result; the onus of proof on fraud is entirely lies upon the defendants that the deed of agreement is not genuine; but the defendants have hopelessly failed to discharge their onus of proof by any tangible evidence. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that vis-à-vis, the plaintiff to the suit to substantiate his claim examined 04 witnesses, who have successfully proved the case of the plaintiff and that the executant of the deed of agreement alleged that he had no title and possession over the suit land and the possession was handed over to the defendants No.3-8, but the 'sole-decree' of Title Suit No. 367 of 1967 speaks that the suit land belonged to the defendant No.1 not to the defendants No.3-8. The learned Advocate lastly submits that without setting aside the aforesaid decree the defendants No.3-8 are debarred from challenging the case of the plaintiff that the defendant No.1 being the owner of the suit land transferred the same in favour of the plaintiff by dint of a deed of agreement. In the 'sole-decree' 2.55 acres of land goes in favour of the defendant No.1 Narayan Chandra and the witness No.2 of the defendant admits that the 'sole-decree' was given on 06.03.1968 and in respect of the kabala deeds of the defendants No.3-8 vide Exhibit-`Ga' series, not a single competent witness have been examined and the learned trial court in his observation and findings adverting evidence on records rightly decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiff. But the appellate court without reversing the findings of the trial court adverting evidence therein, reversed the judgment of the trial court arbitrarily, which is violative to the provision laid down in Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

	11. As against the aforesaid submission, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court during disposal of the appeals committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit as instituted by the plaintiff was time barred and there is no satisfactory explanation or reason from the side of the plaintiff as to why he kept his silence after 1984. In the year 2001 after a long lapse of time the suit was filed which was highly doubtful. The learned Advocate also submits that after 17 years the suit was filed on false allegations on the basis of a forged deed of agreement and the Appellate Court rightly relied upon the maxim of specific performance of contract that 'delay defeats equity'. The learned Advocate further submits that in the binanama there is no specification of the land and in page No.3 of the bainanama there is a mention of the year 2001, which is the crack of the case. The learned appellate court rightly disbelieved the bainanama of the year 1984 which is a forged document and on the basis of a forged document the plaintiff is not entitled a decree for specific performance of contract. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the defendant No.1 had no title and interest over the suit land and the contract as alleged from the side of the plaintiff bears no value in the eye of law and inasmuch as the plaintiff is not coming in clean hands, he is not entitled to get the decree as prayed for. The learned appellate court after thorough evaluation of the evidence on record rightly decided the merit of the appeals in favour of the appellants and allowed both the two appeals in favour of the defendants and there is no infirmity or misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

	12. In order to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocates, having gone through the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.14 of 2001 and the Title Appeal No.33 of 2006 along with 40 of 2006 as well as the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties with all other connected papers and the case records it transpires that it is the positive contention of the plaintiff in his pleading that the defendant No.1 being the owner of the suit property described in the schedule of the plaint entered into a deed of agreement in respect of transfer of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff by virtue of a deed of agreement and it was the contract between the parties that, out of the total consideration amount of Tk.3,75,000/-, Tk.3,60,000/- will be paid by 27.05.1984 and the plaintiff to the suit by the date fixed paid the amount and accordingly a deed of agreement was executed by the defendant No.1 in his favour followed by delivery of possession of the suit property. 

	13. On perusal of the plaint as well as the connected documents I find that the corresponding S.A. khatians No.221, 223, 419 and 467 were prepared in the name of one Monindra Chandra and Narayan Chandra Mondal. The contract between the parties was held on 15.05.1984 and the consideration amount was fixed at Tk.3,75,000/-. It is further contention of the plaintiff that on several occasions he went before the defendant No.1 and requested him to execute and register a sale deed in his favour after taking the remaining sum of Tk.15,000/- and lastly on 05.02.2001 when the plaintiff went to the owner Narayan, it was decided between them that on 14.02.2001 the defendant No.1 coming to the concern Hajiganj police station from his residence of Tongibari police station under Munshiganj District, taking the remaining amount of consideration will execute and register a sub-kabala deed on the following day i.e. 15.02.2001, but while the defendant did not appear according to their agreement, the plaintiff finding no other alternative instituted the original suit on 02.04.2001. It further appears from the schedule of the plaint that the land included within the deed of agreement has been specified in the schedule. In the case records it is noticed that the attorney of the defendant No.1 at first filed a written statement in which he has admitted the deed of agreement between the parties in respect of transfer of the suit land by the defendant No.1 in favour of the plaintiff. The 2nd written statement which was filed by the son of the defendant No.1 after cancellation of the power of attorney goes to show that the deed of agreement has been challenged by the subsequent attorney viz. the son (D.W.1) of the defendant No. 1. 

	14. To substantiate the respective cases of the parties the parties to the suit examined several witnesses. Among them P.W.1 is the plaintiff himself Abul Kalam Azad. This witness in his testimony specifically testified that the concerned S.A. record has been prepared in the name of his vendor Narayon Chandra and Monindra. He has corroborated his plaint case in his examination-in-chief and specifically testified that by way of a deed of agreement dated 27.05.1984 he paid 3,60,000/- and on the very date the possession was delivered in his favour in front of the witnesses namely Tapan, Kuddus, Helu Mia and Hasan Raja. It was further testified by the plaintiff in his deposition that he is still continuing the possession of the suit property. He has developed the land at a expenditure of huge amount of money. With regard to his cause of action he has corroborated his plaint case stating that, finally while on 15.02.2001 the defendant No.1 did not appear before the concern Sub-registry office, he became sure that the defendant will not execute and register a sale deed in his favour. 

	During cross-examination P.W.1 testified at a stage in a reply to a question from the side of the defendants that on 26.05.1984 the stamp paper of bainapatra was purchased in his name. He has denied that the stamp and cartridge paper are anti-dated. With regard to the execution of bainanama P.W.1 testified in his testimony that the defendant told the scribe of the bainapatra and he (P.W.1) accompanied the defendant. At about 12/12.30 p.m. the deed of agreement was written and the witnesses of the deed of agreement put their signatures in different pens. On the date of writing of the deed he paid Tk.3,60,000/- in favour of the defendant and that was kept in seven bundles and all of these are of Tk.500/- notes and the possession was delivered on the same dated at 2.30/3.00 p.m. 

	15. P.W.2 is Hasan Raja, who is one of the witnesses of the deed of agreement. This witness in his testimony specifically testified that he was present at the time of talk of sale between the parties. On 15.05.1984 the consideration amount was fixed at TK.3,75,000/- and on 27.05.1984 the deed of agreement was executed which was written by one Sahadat Moktar. On the very date out of the total consideration amount, Tk.3,60,000/- was paid and this witness as attesting witness put his signature in serial No.2, which has been marked as Exhibit-3(ka) after its proof. This witness also identified the signature of the defendant No.1 which has been marked as Exhibit-4. P.W.2 further testifies that he was present at the time of delivery of possession in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant. 

	During cross-examination in a reply to a question P.W.2 testified at a stage that the deed of agreement after its writing, was read over and after reading the executant put his signature therein. In a reply to another question from the side of the defendants P.W.2 testified that the deed-writer was called by the plaintiff and the defendant who came at 12/12.30 p.m. and this witness was present there till 3.00/3.30 p.m. This witness categorically testified that in plot No.581 the possession was delivered and at that time the land was vacant. 

	16. P.W.3 is another witness of the deed of agreement, who is Helu Mia. This witness in his testimony during his examination-in-chief testified that he was present at the time of talk of sale between the plaintiff and the defendant No.1, of the suit property. The plaintiff and the defendant No.1 is known to him. P.W.3 further testified that the talk of sale was held on 15.05.1984 and the consideration amount was fixed at Tk.3,75,000/-. He was also present on the date of deed of agreement. The defendant No.1 executed the deed of agreement after taking a sum of Tk.3,60,000/- as baina, on the same date. The defendant put his signature in his (P.W.3) presence and he (P.W.3) put his signature as attesting witness in the said deed. P.W.3 identified his signature which has been marked as Exhibit-5. This witness also categorically testified that, on the very date the defendant No.1 handed over possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff and this witness was present at that time. 

	During cross-examination from the side of the defendants, P.W.3 testified at a stage that Narayan Chandra Mondal read the bainapatra and the scribe also read the same. With regard to the possession and identity of the suit land, P.W.3 testified that the possession was delivered in one (khanda', and to the south of plot No.581, one Chand Mia and others possess, to the north Dakatia' river is situated, to the western side college road stands and a sand field of Pourashava lies and to the north side of plot No.579 there is a doba', to the western side college road and to the eastern side there is a pond. In a reply to another question from the side of the defendants No.3-8 this witness testified that on 05.02.2001 he accompanied the plaintiff and went to the defendant No.1 to give him reminder to execute the kabala deed. In another stage of cross-examination this witness testified that the scribe was called by the plaintiff Kalam and the defendant No.1. 

	17. P.W.4 is Md. Sahadat Hossain, who is the scribe of the deed of agreement. This witness in his testimony testified that he knows the parties and there was a deed of agreement among them and he (P.W.4) wrote the same. P.W.4 identified his signature in the deed and also testified in his deposition that after writing of the deed it was read over by him and the defendant Narayan also read the same and on that date the defendant took Tk.3,60,000/- from the plaintiff which is written in the bainapatra. P.W.4 also testified that the deed of agreement is a correct instrument and the executant Narayan Chandra put his signature in presence of the witnesses and the attesting witnesses gave their signatures therein. 

	During cross-examination; P.W.4 testified that in the baina-patra there is a recital, “বায়নাপত্র পাঠ করে অবগত হলাম” This witness also testified that he read over the bainapatra and in the year 1980 he obtained licence of deed writer and finding the C.S. and R.S. khatian the bainapatra was written and the stamp paper of the bainapatra was given to him by both the parties. P.W.4 categorically denied the suggestion of the defendants that the stamp paper was anti-dated. 

	18. On the other hand; from the side of the defendants, D.W.1 Biswanath Mondal is the son of Narayan Chandra Mondal, who on the basis of a power of attorney from his father deposed before the trial court. During his examination-in-chief he has corroborated his written statement which was filed for the 2nd time by himself. This witness testified at a stage that his father Narayan Chandra gave a power of attorney in favour of Jitu Mia who submitted the lg written statement in the original suit. Subsequently; that power of attorney was cancelled by his father by deed No.642 dated 11.10.2001. 

	During cross-examination D.W.1 testify at a stage that his father Narayan Chandra is in his residence and his name is Narayan Chandra Mondal @ Narayan Proshad Mondal. He admits that in Hajiganj police station they had business and landed property and his father obtained the suit land from his grandfather as heir. The land of suit holding corresponds to C.S. khatian No.139 in plot No.581 and in plot No.579 under khatian No.266 and in plot No.577 under khatian No.296. D.W.1 frankly conceded in his deposition that in the S.A. khatian the suit land has been recorded in the name of his father. He also admits in his cross-examination that in partition Suit No.337 of 1967 his father obtained a saham of 2.55 acres of land and prior to this; his father did not transfer his land to anybody. This witness expressed his inability to state anything about the transfer of the suit land by his father in favour of Ali Ahmed Patwary. He has admitted in his cross-examination that in the power of attorney,  which was in favour of Jitu Mia, there is a mention of the suit land and its owner is his father. D.W.1 admitted the signature of his father in the deed of agreement which was signed as "Narayan Chandra Mondal @ Proshad Chandra Mondal." 

	19. D.W.2 is Md. Mizanur Rahman Patwary, who is the defendant No.4. This witness testified in his deposition that his father purchased the land from the defendant No.1. This witness further testified in his examination-in-chief that the defendant No.1 had no title, interest in the suit land at the time of deed of agreement. 

	During cross-examination in a reply to a question D.W.2 testified at a stage that his father obtained property from the defendant No.1 by way of soknama' and his father did not purchase the land by any deed. 

	20. D.W.3 is Abu Taher Majumder, who is the possession witness of the defendants... This witness in his testimony in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiff testified that the suit is for 49Y2 decimals of land and he cannot say the khatian number but the plot number is 581. He has heard that Narayan Chandra was the owner of the suit property. In another stage of his testimony this witness testified that he cannot say the total area of plot No.581 and also cannot say as to whether any other plot is included within the suit property. This D.W.3 in his deposition categorically admitted that he cannot say who possess what land of the suit khatian. 

	21. D.W.4 is Ibrahim Khalil. This witness in his testimony testified that the defendants No.3-8 are his co-sharers and the suit land is situated at Hajiganj Bazar, wherein; Ali Ahmed had business. This witness testified in his examination-in-chief about the possession of the plaintiffs. 

	During cross-examination in a reply to a question D.W.4 testified that his application for becoming party to this suit was rejected by the court which was given in the name of his wife. He does not know anything about the deed of agreement between the plaintiff and Narayan Chandra and also cannot say the number of the suit khatian. He expressed his inability to state in how many khatians the suit land is situated. This witness in his testimony frankly conceded that he cannot say the area of land of each khatian and admitted in his deposition that the owner of the suit khatian was Narayan Chandra Mondal and this suit arise out of the land of Narayan Chandra and in the last portion of his cross-examination this witness testified that he cannot say the area, khatian number and plot number of the suit property. 

	22. In the original suit, one formal witness who is a `mohorar' of Comilla Sadar Joint Sub-registry office deposed as P.W.5, who is Anil Chandra Biswas. This witness testified that he has brought the volume book No.30 and in this book there is an entry of deed No.3186, but there is no consistency with the contents of this deed with the alleged certified copy, which is mentioned in page No.45-48 of the volume book with the certified copies of the same, but in volume book No.6, the certified copy of deed No.877 is consistent with the entry and the contents of deed No.557 of the certified copy is not consistent with the volume book and the certified copy of deed No.5142 is also not consistent with the volume book. Lastly; in comparison with the volume book No.41 the P.W.5 testifies that, there is no consistency of deed No.5127 which is produced as certified copy from the side of the defendants with the concerned volume book. This witness was not cross-examined from the side of the defendants. 

	23. On meticulous evaluation and assessment of the evidence on records, I find in the consultation with the relevant papers that the learned trial court in his observation and findings with regard to the matter of adjudication between the parties as to the deed of agreement between the parties which is the issue No.3 has arrived at a conclusive decision after elaborate discussions and findings with proper sifting of evidence led from the sides of the respective parties. The circumstantial evidence also has been properly pointed out by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in her observation, findings and decision. The conduct of the parties especially the defendant No.1, who was the owner of the suit property the order-sheets as cited by the learned courts below is very much material and important in a suit for specific performance of contract and it has also been properly addressed and apprised by the learned trial court, but the learned appellate court has totally failed to appreciate that, rather; without rebutting those findings and decision; adverting evidence reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court as a whole; which is an apparent illegality on the face of the records. 

	24. With regard to the point of limitation, I have come across from the case records that the learned trial court rightly opined that the plaintiffs to the suit has a definite cause of action and when from the conduct of the defendant Narayan Chandra it has become evident that the defendant has denied to execute and register a transfer deed in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff finding no other alternative filed the suit. 

	25. Under the purview of section 12 of the Specific Relief Act (I of 1877) in a suit for specific performance of contract relating to immovable property, time is not the essence of the contract, nor hardship of the defendant is a ground to refuse relief Our lordships in the case of Anwara Begum Md. Karimul Haque and others 5 BLC (AD)119 held that, the point of limitation is not at all the essence of the suit for specific performance of contract. Besides this; when a vendor executes' a deed of sale but it remains unregistered and the vendee sues for specific performance of the original contract, the question is to be considered whether there is a subsisting contract for sale or not and if the contract be subsisting, the vendee has a statutory right to have the contract performed. 

	26. Under the ambit of section 27 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 Specific Performance inasmuch as is an equitable relief, it is discretionary power of the court and the discretion cannot be exercised arbitrarily and must be exercised judiciously. Here in this case, the conduct of the defendants has played a significant role to disbelieve their case and believe the case of the plaintiff, which has been ignored by the court of appeal below. 

	27. Apart from this, the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur at the time of deciding the merit of the appeal failed to appreciate the actual proposition of law and being guided by surmise and conjecture without adverting and analyzing the evidence on records in its true perspective arrived at an erroneous decision as to the fate of the appeals and thereby committed an error of law. Furthermore, non-consideration of material facts and evidence on records by the learned appellate court has resulted an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, for which the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law as well as in facts. 

	28. It is required to be mentioned here that on my anxious consideration and evaluation of the evidences on records, I find that the plaintiff's witnesses despite have been thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the defendants, but none of them appears to have been discredited. Except some minor discrepancy no such material contradiction or omission is noticed in their testimonies, by which they can be disbelieved and the P.Ws. are competent, credible and trustworthy in comparison with the defendant's witnesses, those who have been contradicted one another in vital facts and their evidence has become shaky in the cross-examination. Moreover, the defendant's witnesses, especially; D.W. 1 Bishwanath Mondol, son of the defendant No.01 is self-contradictory. 

	29. Having regard to the decisions referred to from the sides of the respective parties I have every reason to inclined such a view that the decisions referred to from the side of the opposite parties are not identical and consistent with the instant case- due to its distinguishable facts and characteristics. Besides this, I have already spelt out earlier that in this case, the matter of adjudication between the parties have not been properly and legally resolved by the Appellate Court and by-passing the material evidence on records arbitrarily decided the merit of the appeals and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court which is well reasoned, lawful and consistent with the case records. 

	30. In the foregoing narrative; considering the facts, circumstances, evidence and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule has got much merit to succeed. 

	31. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 16.06.2009 and 22.06.2009 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in allowing the Title Appeal No.33 of 2006 along with Title Appeal No.40 of 2006 analogously and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2006 and 09.04.2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in decreeing the Title Suit No.14 of 2001 is hereby set aside. 

	32. The judgment and order will govern both the two appeals being Title Appeal No.33 of 2006 and Title Appeal No.40 of 2006 simultaneously. 

	33. However; there will be no order as to costs. 

	34. Communicate the judgment and order at once and send down the Lower Court's Records immediately. 

	End.
